summary: Specifies how to signal pseudowire status messages over an associated channel, for static pseudowires that have no dynamic control plane. It also updates RFC 5885 when BFD is used for status signaling. It was later updated by RFC 7274.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6478 specifies how a static pseudowire can report its status to the other endpoint. It sends status messages over an associated channel and repeats them so the other endpoint can detect a missing update.

questions: how does pw status signaling work
what is the pw oam message
subtitle: Carry pseudowire status messages over an associated channel when the pseudowire has no dynamic control plane.

tldr.problem: A statically configured pseudowire has no control plane to report status between its endpoints.
tldr.mechanism: The endpoints send PW OAM messages containing status TLVs over the pseudowire's associated channel and repeat them using a refresh timer.
tldr.outcome: Static pseudowires can exchange status and support related OAM and redundancy procedures. RFC 6478 updates RFC 5885 and is updated by RFC 7274.

today: RFC 6478 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2012. It updates RFC 5885 and the unit metadata says RFC 7274 updates it.

sections.title: Status for Static Pseudowires
sections.content:
A pseudowire set up with LDP has a control plane for signaling its status. A statically configured pseudowire has no such control plane, so its provider-edge endpoints need another way to exchange status.

This RFC carries existing pseudowire status codes in-band with pseudowire data, using the generic associated channel. It also allows a terminating provider-edge node to send a status message directly to the far-end endpoint in the optional bypass mode.
sections.plainLanguage: A manually configured pseudowire has no control channel to report a fault. This RFC gives its endpoints a status message that travels with the pseudowire traffic.

sections.title: When to Use This Status Method
sections.content:
A provider-edge device that creates a pseudowire without LDP MUST support an alternative status-reporting method. This RFC specifies one method for statically configured pseudowires.

A pseudowire established with LDP MUST use the LDP status TLV method and MUST NOT also use this method, to prevent duplicate or conflicting notifications. The optional S-PE bypass mode is an exception. BFD VCCV status signaling types 0x08 and 0x20 also MUST NOT be used at the same time, although BFD VCCV fault detection may still be used.
sections.plainLanguage: Use this method when a pseudowire has no LDP control plane. Do not run two methods that report the same status on one pseudowire, because their reports could conflict.

sections.title: The PW OAM Message Format
sections.content:
The message carries a pseudowire status TLV inside a PW OAM message on the associated channel. The associated-channel header begins with nibble 0001; the version and reserved fields are zero, and the PW OAM Message code point is 0x0027.

The header also contains a refresh timer in seconds, a TLV length, and an acknowledgment flag. A refresh value from 1 through 65535 sets the interval; zero means infinity, so the message is not refreshed and does not time out. The status TLV type is 0x096A.
sections.plainLanguage: The message header identifies PW OAM and gives a refresh interval. Its TLV carries the status being reported, and an acknowledgment flag can confirm receipt.

sections.title: Repeating, Refreshing and Clearing Status
sections.content:
There is no TCP/IP session for these messages, so the sender repeats a new or changed status. It sends the message immediately, then repeats it twice more at one-second intervals if it has not been acknowledged. After those attempts, it sends at the refresh interval; the suggested default is 600 seconds.

The receiver starts a timer from the refresh value. If no new non-zero status message arrives within 3.5 times that value, the status times out and zero is assumed. To clear a fault, the sender sends the status with its bit cleared. A PW OAM status message MUST NOT be used as a connectivity verification method.
sections.plainLanguage: A sender repeats a changed status quickly and then sends refreshes at the agreed interval. If updates stop for long enough, the receiver treats the status as zero.

sections.title: Sending to a Neighbor or the Far Endpoint
sections.content:
Normally a status message is sent to the adjacent provider-edge device across the packet-switched network tunnel, with the pseudowire label TTL set to 1. If the pseudowire does not use a control word, the sender MUST also place the GAL reserved label below the pseudowire label, with TTL 1.

In optional S-PE bypass mode, a terminating provider-edge device sends directly to the far endpoint, skipping switching provider-edge devices. Both endpoints MUST support the mode. Only four listed status codes may be sent this way, and the same status must also be sent through LDP to keep switching devices informed.
sections.plainLanguage: Normally, each status message goes to the next provider-edge device. In bypass mode, supported status messages can go directly to the far endpoint while LDP still informs switching devices.

sections.title: Switching Between Pseudowire Segments
sections.content:
A switching provider-edge device follows the segmented-pseudowire procedures, with additional handling for static segments. When it switches between two static segments, it replaces the LDP header with the PW OAM header while leaving the rest of the packet format the same.

For a dynamic LDP segment connected to a static segment, if the adjacent device withdraws the LDP label, the switching device sets the status to Pseudowire Not Forwarding on the static segment.
sections.plainLanguage: A switching device translates the status format when a static pseudowire meets another kind of segment. If an LDP label is withdrawn, it reports that the static segment is not forwarding.

sections.title: Security and Registered Values
sections.content:
The RFC relies on security measures described in the referenced pseudowire and OAM specifications. It does not add a separate security mechanism.

IANA assigned associated channel type 0x0027, switching-point TLV type 0x07, and pseudowire interface parameter type 0x18. The RFC also defines a registry for generic protocol flags.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC uses the security measures of the related pseudowire protocols. IANA assigned identifiers for the new message and signaling fields.
